::: {#rem-lambda-calculus}
#### Where the name comes from

The word `lambda` comes from the lambda calculus,
a model of computation in which a function is written $\lambda x.\, e$,
the function that takes $x$ to the value of the expression $e$.
The lambda calculus has only three features:
functions, applying a function to an argument, and variables.
It has no numbers, strings or loops [@crichton2019cs242].
Applying $\lambda x.\, e$ to an argument replaces each $x$ in $e$ by that argument,
as in evaluation by substitution (@exm-substitution).
The function in @exr-pair-with that squares its argument is $\lambda x.\, x \cdot x$.

:::

*Media:* Will Crichton's [notes on the lambda calculus](https://stanford-cs242.github.io/f19/lectures/02-1-lambda-calculus), from Stanford's CS 242, *Programming Languages*, go further [@crichton2019cs242].
